_readme.purpose: India-first pathway library for the AI Entrepreneurship Readiness & Pathway Navigator.
_readme.rule: The app may use verified facts below, but must not promise eligibility, funding approval, or successful outcomes. Final decisions remain with the relevant government agency, bank, lender or programme.
changes_v1_1: Added PMEGP application and how-to-apply URLs (supplied by user)
Added PMFME registration URL (supplied by user)
SVEP entry route rewritten as community-based (CRP-EP / BRC); no individual online form
MUDRA entry route: apply through any participating lender; official DFS page kept as source
Added training_pathways and training_links so training becomes a step in the route
Added money_0 routing rule and minimum own-contribution fields
unconfirmed: URLs added in v1.1 were supplied by the user and have not been opened by Claude

SVEP how-to-apply detail comes from secondary sources (schemeinfo.com, iie.gov.in, a research paper, Kudumbashree). Confirm with a Block Resource Centre or DAY-NRLM page before the app states it as fact.
MUDRA: many banks offer their own Mudra forms online (user report); no single central form.

pathways.target_user: People who want to learn how to start a business, including people with an early-stage idea
pathways.eligibility: Startup India describes the program as a free online entrepreneurship program for people seeking to develop ideas and ventures.

entry_route.application_method: Enrol through Startup India Learning & Development

pathways.preparation_needed: None; suitable as an early preparation door.
pathways.why_it_may_fit: Best when the user says: I do not know where to start, has little/no money, or needs basic entrepreneurship knowledge.
pathways.why_it_may_not_fit: It provides learning, not direct funding.
pathways.next_step: Open the official learning page and begin the structured program.
pathways.verification_notes: Official Startup India pages confirm the program is free, online, four weeks, and available in Hindi or English.

pathways.pathway_type: Business support + mentoring + finance access + training
pathways.target_user: Rural people starting or developing early-stage enterprises, especially within the DAY-NRLM ecosystem

money_fit.own_money_required: Not necessarily; support is designed for people facing resource barriers

what_it_provides: Training in business management and soft skills
Guidance for convergence with other government schemes
pathways.eligibility: Access depends on the local SVEP/DAY-NRLM implementation and community ecosystem. The app must verify local availability rather than assume coverage.
requirements: Local programme/community entry point may be required

entry_route.application_method: No open individual online application. Support is routed through community institutions under DAY-NRLM.
how_to_approach: Contact the local Community Resource Person - Enterprise Promotion (CRP-EP) or the Block Resource Centre (BRC) in the project block
Selection is by community organisations (SHG, Village Organisation, Cluster Level Federation) based on need and entrepreneurial potential
CRP-EP helps prepare a business plan and viability test
If viable, support is processed through the Community Enterprise Fund or linked financial institutions
entry_route.portal_note: svep.nrlm.gov.in is a management portal for state and field officers, not an individual application login.

pathways.preparation_needed: Be ready to describe the business idea and local circumstances.
pathways.why_it_may_fit: Strong fit for a rural user with little money, little network, low confidence, and a need for both business guidance and finance access.
pathways.why_it_may_not_fit: Availability and local access depend on programme coverage and implementation.
pathways.next_step: Ask the local SHG, Village Organisation or Block Resource Centre whether SVEP runs in the block, and ask for the CRP-EP.
pathways.verification_notes: Official SVEP portal was last updated 2026-01-19 and describes early/new rural enterprise support, mentoring, finance access, training and banking access.
pathways.target_user_detail: Members of Self-Help Groups and their family members starting or expanding non-farm rural enterprises; sources state at least 60% of beneficiaries should be women (confirm).

pathways.pathway_type: Funding: bank loan + government margin-money subsidy
pathways.target_user: Individuals and eligible organisations establishing new micro-enterprises in rural or urban India
pathways.sector: Manufacturing and service/business, subject to the scheme's eligible-activity/negative-list rules

money_fit.bank_finance: Balance of eligible project cost, subject to bank appraisal

what_it_provides.other: Bank finance plus government margin-money subsidy.

eligibility: Individual applicant must be above 18 years
No income ceiling for setting up projects
For projects above ₹10 lakh in manufacturing or above ₹5 lakh in service/business, at least VIII-standard education is required
Assistance is for new projects; existing units already covered by specified government subsidy schemes are not eligible
requirements: Other documents required by the application/bank

training.name: Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP)
training.required: Mandatory for claiming margin-money subsidy, subject to stated exemptions
training.duration: At least 5 days for projects up to ₹5 lakh; at least 10 days above ₹5 lakh; no EDP mandatory for projects up to ₹2 lakh

entry_route.application_method: Apply on the official PMEGP portal; the application is then processed through implementing agencies and banks.

pathways.preparation_needed: Define the product/service, customer, estimated project cost, funding need and basic business plan.
pathways.why_it_may_fit: Useful when the user has a defined new business and needs financing beyond their available cash.
pathways.why_it_may_not_fit: It is a formal finance pathway and may be premature for an untested idea or a user who is not yet ready with a project proposal. PMEGP covers manufacturing and service units. A shop that only buys and sells goods (trading) may not be eligible, so confirm the activity first.
pathways.next_step: Build a simple project plan and check whether the proposed activity is eligible before applying.
pathways.what_to_say: I want to start [business]. I need approximately [amount] for [specific uses]. My expected customers are [customers], and I can contribute [amount/percentage].
pathways.verification_notes: Current KVIC PMEGP guideline material confirms the ₹50 lakh/₹20 lakh ceilings, contribution and subsidy rates, eligibility conditions and EDP rules.
pathways.scope_caution_to_verify: Added 2026-11-02 as a caution only. Check the PMEGP guidelines for whether trading/retail is eligible, then update this record.

pathways.target_user: Micro enterprises needing working capital or term finance for eligible income-generating activities
pathways.sector: Non-farm income-generating activities, including specified allied agricultural activities

loan_categories.tarun_plus: Above ₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh for entrepreneurs who have successfully repaid a previous Tarun loan, subject to scheme rules

pathways.eligibility: Eligibility and lending decisions are made by the participating lender under PMMY rules and the lender's appraisal.
requirements: Any quotations or financial information requested by the lender

entry_route.application_method: Apply through a participating lender (bank, MFI or NBFC). Many lenders have their own Mudra forms, some online. Do not present MUDRA as a single central lender.
entry_route.user_note: mudra.org.in did not open for the user on 2026-10-30; use the DFS page as the official source and ask the lender directly.

pathways.preparation_needed: Know exactly what the finance will purchase and prepare a simple income/repayment explanation.
pathways.why_it_may_fit: Useful for a user who needs a relatively small amount for equipment or working capital and does not have collateral.
pathways.why_it_may_not_fit: The lender still performs its own appraisal and can decline an application.
pathways.next_step: Define the exact amount needed, what it will buy, and the expected repayment source; then approach a participating lender.
pathways.what_to_say: I need ₹[amount] for [specific purpose]. I expect to earn from [activity] and plan to repay from [income source].
pathways.verification_notes: Current Department of Financial Services information confirms the four categories, lender channels and collateral-free nature of PMMY.

pathways.pathway_name: PMFME (PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises)
pathways.target_user: Individual entrepreneurs and eligible groups/enterprises setting up or upgrading micro food-processing activities

money_fit.beneficiary_contribution: Minimum 10% of project cost for the individual-unit credit-linked subsidy component
money_fit.bank_loan: Balance required funding, subject to bank appraisal

what_it_provides: Credit-linked capital subsidy of 35% of eligible project cost, up to ₹10 lakh per individual unit, subject to scheme conditions
Handholding and DPR support through the implementation ecosystem
pathways.eligibility: Official scheme guidance supports both new and existing micro food-processing enterprises, subject to eligible activities and applicable scheme conditions. ODOP products receive preference, while other eligible micro food enterprises may also be considered.
requirements: Applicable food/business registrations and regulatory requirements
Additional documents requested by the implementing agency/bank

entry_route.application_method: Register on the PMFME portal and work with the state nodal / implementation ecosystem; confirm the local process before acting.

pathways.preparation_needed: Define the food product, target customer, approximate production scale, equipment/working-capital needs and applicable regulatory requirements.
pathways.why_it_may_fit: Strong fit for a food-processing idea where the user needs capital, training and formalisation support.
pathways.why_it_may_not_fit: The proposed activity must be eligible under the scheme; the app should check the activity and local implementation route rather than promise eligibility. PMFME supports micro food-processing units, meaning making or processing food products. A tea stall, restaurant or shop that only sells food or drinks may not be eligible, so confirm this first.
pathways.next_step: Identify the product/activity and state, then verify the applicable PMFME route and eligible activity before preparing the finance proposal.
pathways.what_to_say: I want to start/upgrade a micro food-processing activity producing [product]. I need support for [equipment/working capital/training] and want to understand the PMFME route available in my area.

official_sources.label: MoFPI — Individual Micro Food Processing Units

pathways.verification_notes: Official MoFPI/PMFME sources confirm support for new and existing micro food-processing enterprises and the 35%/₹10 lakh individual-unit credit-linked subsidy with minimum 10% beneficiary contribution.
pathways.scope_caution_to_verify: Added 2026-11-02 as a caution only. Check the PMFME guidelines/FAQ for whether food service or retail is eligible, then update this record.

not_first_doors.reason: Not a first door for a person who only has an idea. Current official scheme rules require a DPIIT-recognised startup and other incorporation/eligibility conditions.
not_first_doors.routing_instruction: Consider after the user has progressed to formal startup setup and meets the current SISFS conditions.

principles: Recommend pathways based on the user's situation, not by displaying a long scheme list.
Never say 'you qualify' unless an official authority has confirmed eligibility.
Use 'this may fit' and explain what must still be confirmed.
Show the official source and last_verified date for every pathway.
If local coverage or lender appraisal is required, say so explicitly.
If a pathway is a later-stage door, do not show it as the user's first action.
Money: compare the user's available money with the pathway's minimum contribution percentage. Compute and show the implied project size as an illustration only, never as a promise.

rules.reason: These require a beneficiary contribution (PMEGP 5-10%, PMFME minimum 10%). Start with learning_program and svep, then revisit.

rules.precondition: Check the food activity and local implementation route.

training_pathways.name: Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) under PMEGP
training_pathways.when_required: Mandatory to claim the margin-money subsidy, with stated exemptions (none mandatory up to Rs 2 lakh)
training_pathways.duration: At least 5 days up to Rs 5 lakh; at least 10 days above Rs 5 lakh
training_pathways.route_position: PMEGP application -> EDP -> project / bank processing
training_pathways.how_to_access: UNCONFIRMED: ask the PMEGP implementing agency or district office when the application is processed

training_pathways.name: PMFME training and capacity building
training_pathways.how_to_access: UNCONFIRMED: through the state nodal / implementation ecosystem
